title: Revit 2026 STALE BUILD warning never cleared on an opted-in year: the bridge DLL was locked before the loader synced (FIXED 28 Oct: loader be58513, bridge 1.0.58)
symptom: Revit's KOR tools work normally but the stale-build warning never clears: C:\ProgramData\KOR\logs\KOR-<date>.log logs "STALE BUILD: running '<old stamp>' but the share has '<new stamp>'. Close ALL Revit 2026 windows and relaunch - the update retries at startup" on every single launch, and following that instruction can never clear it.
cause: In %APPDATA%\Autodesk\Revit\Addins\<year>, KOR.Drafter.addin sorts before KOR.RevitTools.addin and Revit loads add-ins in that order. The Drafter manifest pointed at %LOCALAPPDATA%\KOR\RevitTools\<year>\KOR.Drafter.Bridge.dll - a file inside the loader's own cache - so Revit had loaded and locked it before the loader's sync ran, and the loader's copy failed with "being used by another process". Since version.txt is stamped only if EVERY file copied, the stamp stayed old permanently. Only a year opted in via build\Install-BridgeManifest.ps1 was affected. (A second Revit window of the same year causes a TRANSIENT form of the same lock on machines not opted in: card 36.)
check: C:\ProgramData\KOR\logs\loader.log - look for "copy skipped for KOR.Drafter.Bridge.dll" followed by "cache NOT stamped current". Then compare %LOCALAPPDATA%\KOR\RevitTools\<year>\version.txt against <share>\current\<year>\version.txt, where the share root is the one line in kor-deploy.path beside the loader DLL (currently \\Kor-fs01\Drafting\KOR-Deploy). Affected = a machine whose %APPDATA%\Autodesk\Revit\Addins\<year>\KOR.Drafter.addin points into %LOCALAPPDATA%\KOR\RevitTools\ (after the fix: into its bridge\<git>\ subfolder). Fleet sweep for this: Operations tools/NetworkOpsMaint/revit-cache-state.ps1 (read-only, every profile and year). 27 Oct sweep: 1 of 31 machines read is opted in (KOR-302N 2026). Verified NOT opted in on 2026-10-27: KOR-307-N (3 of 3 manifests point at %LOCALAPPDATA%\KOR.Drafter\<year>) and KOR-306 (2 of 2) - Revit Fleet actions 11491/11497/11498, NetworkOps reads 11478/11495.
fix: SHIPPED and proven 28 Oct (Revit Fleet, oversight commitment 65): the loader be58513 (KOR.RevitTools) installed on KOR-302N 00:0x, and bridge 1.0.58 published 00:10 (stamp 1.0.0+2026-10-28T00:10:08, git be58513); the share's loader folder was refreshed, so new machines onboard with it. The opted-in manifest now points at a VERSIONED folder, %LOCALAPPDATA%\KOR\RevitTools\<year>\bridge\<git>\KOR.Drafter.Bridge.dll, so a running Revit never holds the file being replaced. Evidence (Revit Fleet): launch 1 00:02:43 no "copy skipped", version.txt advanced; launch 2 "Bridge 1.0.57 up"; launch 3 staged be58513; launch 4 00:15:34 "Bridge 1.0.58 up", ping {"bridge":"1.0.58","revit":"2026"}; 0 STALE lines on 28 Oct vs 7 of 7 skipped launches on 27 Oct. Read independently by NetworkOps 28 Oct 00:17 (action 11507): 302N 2026 cache stamp = share stamp be58513; manifest -> RevitTools\2026\bridge\be58513\KOR.Drafter.Bridge.dll; the newest skip lines in loader.log are from 27 Oct 22:45. KNOWN LIMIT: every publish takes one Revit launch to stage it and one to load it.
plain: Explains why Revit on 302N kept saying its KOR tools were out of date even after a restart, and that it was fixed on 28 Oct (loader be58513, bridge 1.0.58): after a publish, expect one launch to stage and one to load. Proof of the fault: KOR-302N 27 Oct, 7 of 7 Revit 2026 launches skipped the copy (10:35:25, 11:03:22, 11:08:31, 13:29:20, 13:31:38, 22:22:56, 22:45:38; actions 11450/11451); control Revit 2024 13:37:02 synced with no skip; cache vs share 8 of 10 identical by hash, only KOR.Drafter.Bridge.dll + version.txt differ (11449); exclusive open succeeds with Revit closed (11454).
